title: The volcano that grounded 10 million people 🌋
subject: volcano
description:
Were you stuck somewhere in April 2010? 👇

In April 2010, Iceland's Eyjafjallajökull volcano sent ash over Europe. More than 300 airports closed, 107,000 flights were cancelled in 8 days, and it became the largest air-traffic shutdown since World War II. The reason traces back to British Airways Flight 9 in 1982.

Sources: USGS Volcano Hazards Program, "Ash clouds and air routes: Eyjafjallajökull"; Wikipedia, "Air travel disruption after the 2010 Eyjafjallajökull eruption" (citing EUROCONTROL and IATA)

scenes.text: One volcano emptied the skies over Europe.
On April 14, 2010, Eyjafjallajökull erupted under an Icelandic glacier, and its ash drifted over Europe.
More than 300 airports closed, the largest air shutdown since World War II.
In 8 days, 107,000 flights were cancelled, affecting roughly 10 million passengers.
In 1982, British Airways Flight 9 had flown into ash from Indonesia's Galunggung, and all 4 engines quit.
The crew restarted 3 and landed. That's why regulators took no chances in 2010.
